name: Dorsa Sadigh

department: Computer Science; Electrical Engineering (Senior Fellow, Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence)
research_topics: Interactive robot learning (lab mission statement: 'theoretical foundations and practical algorithms for interactive robot learning')
Learning from diverse sources of data to build sample-efficient, human-aligned, interactive robot policies
Robots that coordinate with, collaborate with, compete with, or influence humans
Reinforcement learning fine-tuning of vision-language-action (VLA) policies
Cross-embodiment transfer and data-centric robot learning
Generalization evaluation for generalist robot manipulation policies
Human-robot interaction and human skill learning
current_direction: RL fine-tuning of pretrained vision-language-action policies for real-robot reliability
Data-centric robot learning: cross-embodiment transfer, data analogies, generated training data
Measuring and characterizing generalization of generalist manipulation policies
Scalable/gamified robot data collection and in-the-wild data flywheels
Human-facing robotics: robot coaches, skill atrophy, personalized collaboration

evidence.title: Do You Really Need to Pretrain Q-Functions for Online RL Fine-Tuning?
evidence.summary: arXiv preprint dated 2026-07-29 (most recent item found). Authors listed on the arXiv abs page: Perry Dong, Ron Polonsky, Dorsa Sadigh, Chelsea Finn. Abstract states that naive Q-function pretraining 'often provides little benefit over random initialization' and proposes Initialization via Policy Ensemble (IPE), which pools rollouts from multiple diverse policies to bootstrap Q-function learning, yielding an average 1.26x improvement over naive Q-function pre-training on continuous control benchmarks.

evidence.title: EXPO-FT: Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning Finetuning for Vision-Language-Action Models
evidence.summary: arXiv preprint dated 2026-05-25. Authors on the arXiv abs page: Perry Dong, Kuo-Han Hung, Tian Gao, Dorsa Sadigh, Chelsea Finn. Abstract describes a system for stable, sample-efficient RL finetuning of pretrained VLA policies, reporting 30/30 successes on manipulation tasks (routing string lights, striking a pool ball, inserting a flower into a wine bottle) within an average of 19.1 minutes of online robot data, with an open-source codebase released.

evidence.title: Grounding Robot Generalization in Training Data via Retrieval-Augmented VLMs
evidence.summary: arXiv abs page dated 2026-03-12; authors Jensen Gao, Dorsa Sadigh, Sandy Huang, Dhruv Shah. Proposes RADAR, a two-stage framework that retrieves relevant training examples using generalist policy embeddings and then uses VLMs to classify what type of policy generalization a given evaluation task requires. OpenAlex records a journal version in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (2026), DOI 10.1109/lra.2026.3726331.
evidence.venue: arXiv preprint; IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L) 2026 per OpenAlex
